messages.subject: Model average using 2-class models
parts:
Hello everyone,

I would like to experiment with my data a model averaging approach to see the differences between using a half-normal model with only one class or with two classes or a average of both. Does anyone have an advice for me on how to do that when averaging over a model with 1 class and another with 2 classes? As the 2-class model comprises 2 sessions, respectively 2 parameter estimates, the model.averaging gives me 2 sigma estimates that are quite different. How is the model average calculated in this case? 

Thanks a lot for any help on this topic!
Chiara

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Model average using 2-class models
parts:
Hello Chiara
I do not have a straight answer and nor it seems does anyone else. The question is outside normal usage (we don't usually want to collapse the heterogeneous sigma to a single average value) and not specific to SECR, so it might help to consult a friendly statistician. Model averaging is not mysterious - you can do it yourself on one line with the AIC model weights and the standard formulae (SE a little harder, but still do-able). I would compute the weighted sigma for the h2 model, as discussed before, and model average that with sigma from the other model.
Murray
